prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Customer Onboarding Field Validation Rules (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Field" · longest unbreakable word 126px · one-line width 126px
  col 2: header "Pattern" · longest unbreakable word 114px · one-line width 1074px
  col 3: header "Example valid" · longest unbreakable word 167px · one-line width 264px
  col 4: header "Error message" · longest unbreakable word 157px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A reference table for developers, QA and support to validate customer-onboarding fields: each row maps a field to its regex rule, a valid example, and the error copy shown on failure.","reading":"Readers look up rows by Field, then scan Pattern for implementation/testing and glance across to Example valid and Error message for concrete values and user-facing wording. Comparison is mainly within each row, not down numeric columns.","groups":["Field is the row key and identifier","Pattern and Example valid belong together as rule plus concrete instance","Example valid and Error message belong together as reader-facing validation feedback","Pattern is the technical column; Example valid and Error message are the human-facing columns"],"keep_intact":["snake_case field identifiers","regex atoms, character classes, quantifiers and anchors without mid-token breaks","example values such as emails, dates, currency amounts, slugs and VAT IDs","header words and error-message words"],"may_wrap":["long Pattern values at regex punctuation, alternation or quantifier boundaries","Error message prose at spaces","Example valid only at safe separators if necessary","multi-word headers at their space"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[147,206,188,178],"idea":"Preserve every longest token in the other columns and give all remaining width to Pattern, minimizing regex wrapping."},{"name":"B","widths":[147,160,210,202],"idea":"Keep the row key and regex legible, then split spare width between Example valid and Error message so both human-facing columns read comfortably."},{"name":"C","widths":[147,135,188,249],"idea":"Hold Pattern at its minimum intact width and spend the width on Error message, since support-oriented prose benefits most from fewer wraps."}]}
